summary: Fine-tuning makes sense when you need to change a model's behavior, style, or format consistently, or when you want to distill a large model's capabilities into a smaller, cheaper one for a narrow task. RAG is the better choice when the problem is about injecting up-to-date or proprietary knowledge that changes frequently, while prompt engineering should always be exhausted first since it is the cheapest and fastest to iterate. In practice, teams often combine fine-tuning for behavior/format with RAG for knowledge grounding.
when_to_fine_tune: Choose fine-tuning when you need consistent output structure, tone, or domain-specific style that prompting alone cannot reliably enforce.
Choose fine-tuning to distill a large, expensive model into a smaller open model that matches quality at lower latency and cost at scale.
Prefer RAG over fine-tuning when the task requires current, frequently-changing, or large-corpus factual knowledge that would be impractical to bake into weights.
Exhaust prompt engineering and few-shot examples first; only fine-tune once you have high-quality labeled examples (typically hundreds to thousands) and a stable, repeatable task.

tools.name: OpenAI Fine-Tuning API
tools.pricing_paid: Pay per token for training plus hosting/inference; e.g. GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4.1 fine-tuning billed per 1M training tokens and per-token inference
features: Integrated eval and validation data support
tools.best_for: Instruction tuning and output-format/behavior control on proprietary GPT models without managing infrastructure

tools.name: Hugging Face AutoTrain
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-as-you-go for managed compute (per GPU-hour on Spaces/Jobs); free locally and with free tier
features: Runs on HF cloud or locally
tools.best_for: Accessible no-code/low-code fine-tuning of open-source models with the broadest model selection

tools.name: Together AI Fine-Tuning
tools.pricing_paid: Pay per token trained plus hosting; transparent per-model pricing with no infra management
features: Serverless and dedicated inference for tuned models
tools.best_for: Production fine-tuning and serving of open-source models without managing training infrastructure

tools.name: Amazon Bedrock Fine-Tuning
tools.pricing_paid: Pay for training (per token/compute) plus provisioned throughput for hosting tuned models
tools.best_for: Enterprise domain adaptation within AWS with strong governance and data residency requirements

tools.name: Google Vertex AI Fine-Tuning
tools.pricing_paid: Pay per training node-hour / tokens plus hosting; GCP consumption billing
tools.best_for: Enterprise tuning of Gemini and open models integrated into Google Cloud workflows

tools.name: Unsloth
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; paid Pro/enterprise tiers for multi-GPU and support
tools.best_for: Fast, memory-efficient local or single-GPU fine-tuning of open models for cost-conscious developers

tools.name: Axolotl
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; compute cost is your own cloud/local GPUs
tools.best_for: Flexible, reproducible open-source fine-tuning and RLHF for ML practitioners who want full control

tools.name: LLaMA-Factory
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; you pay only for your own compute
